doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Eckstine pay, solos and influences
summary: Twenty-five dollars a night with Eckstine playing lead alto, a few solos per band, and influences Hodges, Carter and Willie Smith.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Well by the time you got to the end of the week, what kind of salary were you making in those days?
Well with Billy Eckstine I think I made more than I’d ever made, I made twenty-five dollars a night. Worked almost every night.
I guess for those times that was — you could have done worse.
And you were doing what you liked. Were you playing alto?
How much chance did you get in those bands to get up and solo?
Well I had a few solos in every band I played in. Maybe a ballad or jump blues.
Were there certain artists at the time on record that you were being influenced by?

Oh yeah. As a matter of fact I was always being influenced by Johnny Hodges and Benny Carter and Willie Smith that played lead with Jimmy Lunceford’s band and later on he played with the Harry James band.
